criteria.inclusion_html:
A drug is included when AI or machine learning was used materially in at least one of:

  1. Target identification: the biological target or mechanism was nominated by an AI/ML platform (e.g. Insilico's PandaOmics nominating TNIK for IPF; Recursion's phenomics maps).
  2. Molecule design or optimisation: the chemical or biological structure was generated, prioritised or optimised by AI/ML or large-scale computational physics models (e.g. generative chemistry, protein language models, free-energy-perturbation design at scale).
  3. Repurposing: an existing molecule was matched to a new indication by an AI/ML system, and the company states this (e.g. BenevolentAI and baricitinib for COVID-19). These are tagged ai_role = repurposing so the dashboard can include or exclude them.
  4. Personalised design: the product is designed per patient by an algorithm (e.g. AI-selected neoantigens in cancer vaccines). Tagged ai_role = personalised_design.

Excluded: AI used only in trial operations (site selection, recruitment, digital twins), patient stratification/biomarkers on a conventionally discovered drug (e.g. Alto Neuroscience), or in-licensed assets that an AI-branded company did not design (e.g. most of Formation Bio's and Pathos's in-licensed pipeline).

Must be clinical-stage: at least one human dose in an interventional trial (Phase 1 onwards), including programmes since discontinued, so the dashboard can track attrition as well as progress.
criteria.confidence_html:
LevelMeaning
highThe company or a peer-reviewed publication explicitly states AI/ML designed the molecule or nominated the target.
mediumAsset from an AI-native or computation-first company (or AI repurposing) where AI use is likely but the specific claim for this molecule is not explicit, or the "AI" is mainly physics-based computation (e.g. Schrödinger, Nimbus, Relay).
lowOnly a partnership announcement, press coverage or third-party tracker links the asset to AI; no company or paper claim found.

Flag uncertain entries instead of dropping them: the status or ai_role notes say what still needs checking.
criteria.gaps_html:
• The ASCO and Medspark totals (117 to ~175) are larger than this list because they include many Chinese and undisclosed-code assets whose AI claims could not be checked. Treat this seed list as the verifiable core, and grow it from tracker updates.
  • Seed nct_ids are sparse, but the refresh fills the gap. Only IDs confirmed from press releases or trackers are typed into the seed file; every refresh then queries the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API for each drug's codes and links what it finds, so a blank nct_ids cell does not mean the drug has no trials on the page. Three drugs still resolve to no trial at all, which usually means they are registered outside ClinicalTrials.gov (CTR20 in China, JapicCTI in Japan).
  • 18 rows carry a VERIFY note. scripts/verify.py sorts them by what is actually blocking: five where ClinicalTrials.gov reports a higher phase than the seed list and a human has to confirm which is right, eight asking something a registry cannot answer (an undisclosed target, a filing, whether a company still backs a programme), three with no trials found, and two whose trials give no conclusive status.
  • Edge cases kept but tagged so the dashboard can filter them: AI repurposing of known molecules (baricitinib, REC-4881, REC-994, REC-2282, BXCL501), physics-based computational design (Schrödinger, Nimbus, Relay, Structure), and algorithmic neoantigen vaccines (EVX-01, TG4050, mRNA-4157).

criteria.sources_html:
• Jayatunga et al., "How successful are AI-discovered drugs in clinical trials?", Drug Discovery Today 2024 (BCG/Wellcome), PubMed 38692505: defines AI-native biotech assets; 75 molecules entering clinic 2015–2023.
  • ASCO 2026 abstract 11072 (JCO 44:16 suppl), doi: 117 AI-enabled assets from 63 companies in interventional trials by Dec 2025.
  • Trackers: IntuitionLabs, Medspark, Vision Lifesciences.
  • Company pipeline pages and press releases (linked per row) and ClinicalTrials.gov for NCT IDs.

benchmarks._note: Hand-entered reference rates. Nothing here is computed from the tracker; edit the values and keep the citations honest.

industry.label: Industry baseline (2011-2020)
industry.citation: BIO, Informa Pharma Intelligence and QLS Advisors, Clinical Development Success Rates 2011-2020. Phase 1 52.0%, Phase 2 28.9%, Phase 3 57.8%, filing 90.6%.

ai.label: AI-discovered molecules (BCG/Wellcome 2024)
ai.citation: Jayatunga et al., 'How successful are AI-discovered drugs in clinical trials? A first analysis and emerging lessons', Drug Discovery Today 2024. Phase 1 success 80-90% (n=24); Phase 2 success around 40% (n=10), in line with historical industry averages. Small sample - treat as indicative.

caveats: Benchmark rates are per-phase transition rates for completed programmes. The funnel on this page is a snapshot of a young cohort: most drugs in it have not had the chance to progress or fail yet, so the funnel's stage-to-stage ratios are not success rates.
The 'outcome known' rates on this page use only drugs whose programme has resolved at a phase - progressed beyond it, or stopped at it. Denominators are small; they are shown next to every rate.
